sentences.text: If you dig a gap and lay a plank across it, you have a bridge.
But a car rolls up to the plank and it snaps in the middle.
So you slide steel girders under the plank to carry the load.
But the girders still span a long gap, so you add a pier that holds up the middle.
A car's weight bends the deck, and the top is squeezed while the bottom is stretched.
But when a flood fills the river, the current scours the foot of the pier until it cracks.
So you wrap the pier in concrete and pile rocks round its foot, a standard defence against scour.
And a bridge is not locked rigid in place.
In summer heat, a 100 m steel span grows about 6 cm, so the deck slides.
Add rails, a centre line, a lamp and young trees.
Congratulations, you have built a bridge.
